target_customer: Pharma and biotech partners that would license immune system drug targets, with the company itself as a therapeutics developer
problem: Finding drug targets for immune and inflammatory disease is slow and biased by prior hypotheses. Synkrino proposed an AI system that mines patient immune tissue data for targets without that bias.
business_model: Drug discovery platform feeding an internal therapeutics pipeline, possible partnering

founders.name: David Ott
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no bio. Technical flag inferred from the CTO title on the YC page only.

competitors.name: Atomwise
competitors.what: Deep learning platform for small molecule drug discovery
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the source consulted
competitors.funding_then: Raised a $45M Series A in March 2018, over $51M total

technical_complexity.rationale: Mining patient immune tissue data with neural networks to find novel targets, then validating them biologically, is research grade work for two people.

defensibility.rationale: Any defensibility would come from exclusive patient datasets and validated targets. No source shows data access, patents or partners.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows any incumbent reacting to Synkrino. The company left almost no public trace.

market_need_then: AI drug discovery was surging in 2018, with Atomwise raising a $45M Series A in March 2018 and other AI discovery firms raising large rounds, so investor appetite existed. No source documents specific customer demand for Synkrino.

branding.domain_note: Uses synkrino.bio, not a .com. Site returned HTTP 503 when fetched.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search returned nothing about the company. Aggregators even give the platform two different names (SATIS and AIDE).

outcome_analysis: The outcome is not public. The YC directory marks the company active with two people, while a PitchBook profile lists it as out of business in September 2024. No press, post-mortem or filing was found for either claim, so the cause of any shutdown is not public and no failure factors are asserted. The company is early stage biotech that left almost no verifiable funding or product trail.
notes: Company website returned 503, so it may be dead or down; not worked around. Funding is unverified: CB Insights lists about $120K seed in July 2018 (page slug names a different company), Bouncewatch and Startup Intros mention Endpoint Ventures on 2018-08-23, Dealroom mentions adMare, and PitchBook states $25.1M. These conflict and all come from aggregators, so no round is recorded. A Dealroom entry with different founders appears to belong to another company. Status conflict: directory says Active, PitchBook says out of business 2024-09-06; exit type left unknown. Competitor list is a loose adjacent peer, since no dated immunology specific rival was found. Completeness pass: each round rests on a single database (CB Insights 120K Jul 25 2018, whose page slug names another company; Startupintros/Bouncewatch Endpoint Ventures Aug 23 2018). PitchBook states 25.1M total, so a large gap is known and unresolved; Dealroom mentions adMare.
